frames.S: stand frame, mm: origin on the bench top on the pan axis; x = machine +x (operator's right), y = toward the CNC (machine back), z = up
frames.bench_three: twin bench-top frame (three.js, Y up): (X, Y, Z) = (-x, z, y - 225)
frames.deck: cloud deck coords (bed frame, z up from the bed) at bed machine y = 90: deck = (x + 150, y - 135, z - 72)

pan.positive: counter-clockwise from above (rear camera from the deck toward the operator's left, so_a)
pan.mech_zero: yoke square to the machine: rear camera azimuth +y (machine back)

tilt.angle: el = rear-camera elevation (deg): 0 = phone upright, screen to the operator; -90 = straight down

camera.T: tilt frame at el = 0: origin on the tilt axis, axes = S at pan 0
camera.note: nominal nominal 6.1 in phone (iPhone 15 size) centred by the clamp: main camera 22.0 mm right of the phone centre (seen from the screen), 60.0 mm above it. Measure yours.

reference.note: protocol aim (0, 0) = this pose: pan = pan_mech - pan_mech_ref, tilt = el - el_ref

operator.note: screen (front camera) toward the operator's face

aim_reference_impl: pstand/kin.py aim(): fixed-point iteration putting the target on the camera axis including the camera offset from both axes

cloud_cal_stand.note: values for cloud/src/devices/stand.ts (cal:stand). Its model puts the camera at `pivot`; this is the best-fit single point (S [7.5, 4.0, 441.4], near the tilt axis): max pointing error 2.3 deg over the deck plane and the beaker rims. The exact model above (aim_reference_impl) has none.

keepout_S.note: for the SO-101 planners: the phone sweeps a 95 mm sphere about the tilt axis
